verdict.stance: Neutral / Sovereign Wealth Proxy Funding Vision 2030 (Aa3 / A+)
verdict.summary: PIF holds $904.5bn AUM (SAR 3.4tn) with consolidated FY25 revenue of $120bn (+9%) and net profit doubling to $17bn, underpinned by 100% Saudi sovereign ownership (Aa3/A+). Rising consolidated borrowings (SAR 725.3bn) and heavy domestic giga-project capex as PIF pivots into its 2026-2030 strategy drive persistent multi-currency bond/sukuk supply.

positives: 100% Kingdom of Saudi Arabia sovereign wealth fund (Aa3/A+); core engine of Vision 2030.
$904.5bn AUM with 76% domestic strategic holdings (Aramco 16%, STC, Ma'aden, SNB) and 5.8% TSR since 2017.
FY25 net profit doubled to $17bn on maturing domestic portfolio dividends.
negatives: Consolidated borrowings climbed to SAR 725.3bn (~$193.4bn) funding capital-intensive giga-projects.
Heavy ongoing USD/EUR/Sukuk issuance supply keeps spread compression capped vs sovereign.
Mark-to-market volatility on global listed holdings drove negative other comprehensive income in FY25.

background.business_overview: Sovereign wealth fund of the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia.
background.asset_perimeter: SAR 3.4tn AUM: 76% domestic (SAR 2.57tn), 20% international, 4% treasury; major stakes in Aramco, STC, Ma'aden, ACWA, giga-projects.
background.ownership_governance: 100% State of Saudi Arabia; governed by Council of Economic and Development Affairs.

recent_drivers: Nov-26: S&P Global Ratings assigned PIF its inaugural 'A+' Stable long-term issuer credit rating, completing full three-agency coverage alongside Moody's (Aa3) and Fitch (A+).
Jan-26: Priced $2.0bn 10Y benchmark USD Sukuk due Jan-36 at T+85bps; transition into 2026-2030 strategy.
FY25 Report: AUM $904.5bn, revenue $120bn (+9%), net profit $17bn (SAR 65.2bn), borrowings SAR 725.3bn.
